events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.55 (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The trip ran 2.52 km over the optimal route, well past the 1 km tolerance, and the fare record bills that excess at $1.4100/km [F1][F4][RD-1]. There is one off-route segment, 12:19–12:25, 4.20 km driven over 1.89 km optimal, +2.31 km [F3].

Traffic reason (RD-4) is settled for that segment: Ayer Rajah Expressway, a road on the replaced stretch, was in speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) from 12:06 to 12:25, i.e. active when the segment began, with no separate incident recorded [F11][F14][RD-4]. Under RD-2 a traffic reason changes nothing about the amount: the refund still turns on whether the rider was informed and agreed before the deviation [RD-2][RD-5]. The trace records no driver violation.

Notice and consent (RD-5) fail. The driver's message proposing the reroute via Clementi Avenue 2 came at 12:15, before the 12:19 segment start, so notice in time is not the problem [F7]. The problem is the rider's reply at 12:16: "hmm ok lor" — a resigned, non-committal murmur, not an agreement to a specific named road; the complaint that "I never agreed to any detour, I just said hmm" reads the same words consistently [F8]. It names no road or area, so it is not a specific road agreement, and read as a general choice it would still not cover the driver's route; the driver's own statement that "the rider said ok" is a claim written after the trip and, with a complete two-message chat on record, cannot supply consent [F10][F9][RD-5]. No rider message before the segment names a place or route, so RD-3 does not exempt anything either [F7][F8][RD-3]. The segment therefore counts in full.

Amount: deviation 2.52 km − 0 km exempt = 2.52 km × $1.4100/km = $3.55, matching the billed excess distance [F4][RD-2]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded, and there is no surge here in any event [F5][F6][RD-2]. The refundable amount is under $10 and the dispute is a route deviation on a settled record, so the system decides it [TH-1][TH-2].

The driver's profile shows 2 upheld disputes but none for route deviation, and RD-6 requires a prior upheld route deviation within 90 days, so no account flag is raised; the profile alone never decides this case anyway [F17][RD-6].

RIDER: We've reviewed your dispute and are refunding $3.55.

Your ride went 2.52 km further than the best route — more than the 1 km we allow. We checked the notice rules: a driver must get your agreement to a specific detour before taking it. The message you sent back didn't name a road or area or agree to a route, so it doesn't count as consent.

That $3.55 is the fare for the extra distance and goes back to the method you originally paid with. Tolls, time and any surge aren't refunded. No action is being taken on your account.

DRIVER: We've reviewed this trip and are refunding the rider $3.55.

The ride ran 2.52 km past the best route, above the 1 km tolerance. Before a detour like this, you need the rider's clear agreement to the specific route. Traffic conditions don't change this: the requirement is to inform the rider and get agreement before deviating. The message you sent doesn't count, because the reply didn't name a road or agree to one.

We're sending you a notification-duty reminder and logging this on your route compliance record. It's your first such incident, so there's no warning and no account flag. It just means a repeat could be treated more seriously.

The rider's 12:16 reply "hmm ok lor" does not agree to the driver-proposed route and names no road; the driver's post-trip statement is a claim, not prior rider consent, and the complete chat record contains no rider agreement before the segment [F8][F10][F9][RD-5].

segment_findings.reason: The driver's 12:15 message proposed going via Clementi Avenue 2 but the rider's only reply before the 12:19 segment start, "hmm ok lor", names no road or area and is a non-committal murmur rather than an agreement to the reroute [F7][F8]; the driver's post-trip statement that the rider said ok is a claim, not rider consent, and the complete chat record shows no rider agreement [F10][F9]. No prior rider message names a place or route, so RD-3 does not apply, and the traffic reason never exempts [RD-3][RD-4][RD-5].

? RD-5 rider informed and agreed before the deviation; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent by 12:19:35 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go via X'): put X in named_road; code checks it against the roads this segment drove (FABER DRIVE → JALAN LEMPENG → CLEMENTI AVENUE 6 → COMMONWEALTH AVENUE WEST → CLEMENTI AVENUE 4 → CLEMENTI AVENUE 5 → CLEMENTI AVENUE 2 → WEST COAST ROAD → JUBILEE ROAD): X among them → named_road_tied (exempt), otherwise named_road_elsewhere (counts). (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent; a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F7: Chat #1 12:15 driver: “Jam ahead on Ayer Rajah Expressway, I'm going via Clementi Avenue 2.”; F8: Chat #2 12:16 rider: “hmm ok lor”; F10: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “I told the rider there was a jam on Ayer Rajah Expressway and that I was going via Clementi Avenue 2, and the rider said ok.” (F7, F8, F10)

notices.text:
We've reviewed your dispute and are refunding $3.55.

Your ride went 2.52 km further than the best route — more than the 1 km we allow. We checked the notice rules: a driver must get your agreement to a specific detour before taking it. The message you sent back didn't name a road or area or agree to a route, so it doesn't count as consent.

That $3.55 is the fare for the extra distance and goes back to the method you originally paid with. Tolls, time and any surge aren't refunded. No action is being taken on your account.

We've reviewed this trip and are refunding the rider $3.55.

The ride ran 2.52 km past the best route, above the 1 km tolerance. Before a detour like this, you need the rider's clear agreement to the specific route. Traffic conditions don't change this: the requirement is to inform the rider and get agreement before deviating. The message you sent doesn't count, because the reply didn't name a road or agree to one.

We're sending you a notification-duty reminder and logging this on your route compliance record. It's your first such incident, so there's no warning and no account flag. It just means a repeat could be treated more seriously.
